t: This is 74 Brook Street, a building in Westminster. Sir William Gull, the physician, died here in 1890. He came from a modest family but built a lucrative private practice, and he served as Governor of Guy's Hospital and Fullerian Professor of Physiology. In 1871 he successfully treated the Prince of Wales during a life-threatening attack of typhoid fever. As a result he was made a baronet and appointed one of the Physicians-in-Ordinary to Queen Victoria.
